turns.prompt_text: Was there a shark tank product made and designed to hold many grocery bags, was it shaped like a loop device?
turns.response_html:
Yes, there was a Shark Tank product designed exactly for that purpose. It is called Click & Carry, and while it isn't a simple "loop" like a carabiner, it has a distinct cylindrical, loop-like shape with a rotating mechanism.

The product was featured in Season 12 (2020) by entrepreneur Kim Meckwood, who received a joint deal from Sharks Mark Cuban and Barbara Corcoran.

How it Works

The design is intended to solve the problem of grocery bags cutting into your hands or having to make multiple trips to the car:

  • The Design: It is a handheld device with a padded gel grip. It features two deep side cavities to hold bag handles.
  • The "Loop" Mechanism: The top part of the handle rotates (twists) open to allow you to hook multiple bags into the side channels. You then twist it back to "click" it shut, creating a secure loop that prevents bags from falling out.
  • Hands-Free: One of its standout features is that because of its shape and padding, you can actually wear it over your shoulder, allowing you to carry up to 100 lbs (50 lbs on each side) hands-free.

Other Similar Products

While Click & Carry is the most famous from Shark Tank, there is another product called the Mighty Handle that often gets confused with it. The Mighty Handle is more of a static, anchor-shaped hook, but it does not have the "click-to-close" rotating loop feature that Kim Meckwood’s invention is known for.

Perspective from the "One-Trip" Community

From the perspective of urban dwellers or those living in walk-up apartments, this product has been a massive hit. It’s frequently cited in "life hack" communities as a game-changer for people who live in cities like New York or London, where the "one-trip challenge" is a daily reality of walking from the market to an apartment.
